{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Mexico|Cuisine of Mexico]] | [[Cookbook:Southwestern cuisine|Southwestern U.S. cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Tex-Mex cuisine|Tex-Mex cuisine]]

'''Adobo sauce''' is a sauce or [[Cookbook:Marinating|marinade]] used in Latin American and Southwestern U.S.-style cooking, made of finely chopped or pureed [[Cookbook:Chiles|chiles]], [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], [[Cookbook:Vinegar|vinegar]], and often [[Cookbook:Onion|onions]] and [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]]. Food that has been prepared with adobo is sometimes called ''adobado'' [http://www.cookinglight.com/cooking/cs/techniques/article/0,13803,232455-232428,00.html].

Chipotles in adobo sauce is a particular use of this condiment in which chipotles (smoked jalapeño peppers) are stewed in adobo sauce. Ingredients of this sauce generally include tomatoes, garlic, vinegar, salt, and spices.
  
==Ingredients==

*12 [[Cookbook:Chipotle Pepper|chipotle peppers]] or smoked, dried [[Cookbook:Jalapeño|jalapeño peppers]] (most co-ops can get these for you, or try the specialty produce section of your grocery store)
*4 [[Cookbook:Cup|cups]] (0.95 [[Cookbook:Liter|L]]) water
*½ cup (120 [[Cookbook:Milliliter|ml]]) [[Cookbook:Onion|onion]], [[Cookbook:Dice|diced]]
*⅓ cup (80 ml) [[Cookbook:Vinegar|apple cider vinegar]]
*¼ cup (60 ml) [[Cookbook:Ketchup|ketchup]]
*3 cloves [[Cookbook:Garlic|garlic]], crushed or [[Cookbook:Slicing|sliced]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] of [[Cookbook:Cumin|cumin]], [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]]
*[[Cookbook:Salt|Salt]] to taste

== Procedure ==

# Combine all ingredients in a heavy [[Cookbook:Saucepan|saucepan]]. Cook over a very low heat for 1–2 hours until the chiles are very soft and the liquid has been reduced to about 1 cup. Alternatively, cook in a [[Cookbook:Slow Cooker|slow cooker]] overnight. 
# Beat with a [[Cookbook:Mortar and Pestle|mortar and pestle]], or put in [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]] to [[Cookbook:Purée|puree]] for a thick sauce. 

== Notes, tips, and variations ==
* Sauce will keep for several weeks in the fridge in an airtight container. You can also can it in mason jars for longer storage, following proper procedures for sterilizing jars and [[Cookbook:Canning|canning]].
